seo.title: Website cost calculator
seo.description: Answer eight questions and see an indicative range for your website or platform in under three minutes, with the breakdown and what would move it.

hero.title: Website cost calculator
hero.answer: Most Calwebtech projects run between $12,000 and $60,000: a focused marketing site is $12,000 to $25,000, and a platform build with booking, a dashboard and integrations is $25,000 to $60,000. This calculator asks eight questions about your project and gives you an indicative range in under three minutes, with the breakdown behind it. Ongoing care and development starts from $1,500 a month.
hero.intro: There is no sales call attached to it. Answer the eight questions, see your range on this page, and we will email you a copy with the breakdown so you can share it internally. If the number works, the next step books a consultation with your answers already attached.
points: No sales call needed to see the range

methodology.heading: How do we work the number out?
methodology.intro: The calculator is a published price list, not a black box. Each answer adds a figure from the table below, every line is rounded to the nearest $500, and the lines are added up. The same code produces the range on this page, the copy in your inbox and the figure our own team sees.

sections.heading: Where do the figures come from?
paragraphs: They come from what our projects have cost to deliver, grouped into the two bands we publish: a focused build at $12,000 to $25,000 and a platform build at $25,000 to $60,000. The starting figure for each project type covers discovery, design from our component library, the content management system, lead capture, up to ten pages, testing and launch, so the leanest marketing site begins at the bottom of the focused band. Everything after that is an addition you can see and check.
The rates are versioned. Every estimate is stored with the version of the model that produced it, so a range given today can still be read back against the rates that were in force when it was given.

sections.heading: Why is it a range and not a single price?
paragraphs: Two projects that answer these eight questions identically can still differ by a third once you know how many people have to approve a page, how clean the data in the old system is, or how many edge cases the checkout has. The range is honest about that spread rather than hiding it behind one number.

The low end assumes decisions arrive when we need them and the content is broadly ready. The high end assumes more review rounds, more stakeholders and more to work out along the way. Most projects land between the two.

sections.heading: What is not included in the range?
paragraphs: Hosting, domains, paid plugins and platform licences are billed to you directly and registered in your name, so they are outside the figure here. Paid advertising, photography and video shoots are outside it too. Ongoing care and development is monthly and priced separately, from $1,500 a month.

Nor does it cover work eight questions cannot see: migrating a system nobody has looked at yet, connecting to software with no documented interface, or running the site in several languages. Those are scoped properly and quoted on their own.

sections.heading: How does a range become a fixed price?
paragraphs: On a call and in the proposal that follows it. We go through your answers, look at the parts that carry the risk, which are usually the content structure, the integrations, the data to migrate and the pages that have to convert, and set a fixed price for a fixed scope. The first call and the written proposal are free.

The discovery stage in the first week of the project confirms that scope in writing. After that the price does not move unless the scope does: a change is quoted and waits for your approval before any work starts on it.

sections.heading: What happens to the answers I give?
paragraphs: They are stored in our own PostgreSQL database alongside your enquiry, as eight separate fields rather than a paragraph of notes, so the team can see the shape of your project before the first call. Cloudflare Turnstile checks the form to keep automated submissions out, and Resend is used only to deliver the copy to your inbox.
There is no form vendor, no mailing list platform and no advertising pixel on this page. You can ask us to delete the record at any time, as the privacy policy explains.

sections.heading: Can I check the arithmetic myself?
paragraphs: Yes, and that is what the table below is for. Take the starting figure for your project type, add the amount for each answer you gave, then add the schedule uplift if you chose a launch inside eight weeks. Each line is rounded to the nearest $500 and the total is the sum of the lines, so the breakdown on screen always adds up to the range above it.

methodology.rateIntro: Every figure the calculator can add, in one table. The starting figure for your project type is the beginning; everything else is added to it. Content is priced for a site under ten pages and scales with the page count you choose.

Choosing Shopify for an online store, or a dashboard for a web application, adds nothing, because the starting figure for that project type already covers it. Care plans and the Ongoing partner plan start at $1,500 a month and are quoted separately from the build.

faqs.question: How accurate is a website cost calculator?
faqs.answer: This one is as accurate as eight questions allow, which is enough to tell you whether we are in your range and not enough to sign a contract on. It uses the rates published on this page and the same code our own system uses, so the figure is not a marketing number. Once we have been through your content, your integrations and the data to migrate, the range becomes a fixed price for a fixed scope in the written proposal.

faqs.question: Why do website prices vary so much between agencies?
faqs.answer: Because the word website covers everything from a template filled in over a weekend to a platform with a dashboard, a booking system and a live connection to an inventory system. Rates differ too, and so does what is included: design, content structure, testing, accessibility and performance work are part of the price here rather than extras added later. Comparing quotes is easier when you compare what each scope says it will deliver instead of the number on the front page.

faqs.question: Can we build the site in phases to spread the cost?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. The usual approach is to launch the pages that earn their keep first, then add the sections and integrations that need more working out. Phasing costs a little more in total than one continuous build, because each phase carries its own testing and release, but it moves the spend into a schedule you can plan around.

faqs.question: What is the smallest project you take on?
faqs.answer: Around $12,000, the bottom of the focused band. Below that we cannot do the discovery, design, build, testing and launch properly, and a project done at half attention is worse value than one not started. If your budget is under that figure we will say so on the first call rather than stretch the scope to fit.

faqs.question: Will I get a sales call after using the calculator?
faqs.answer: No. You get the range on this page and a copy by email, and nothing else follows unless you ask for it. If you do book a consultation from the result, the person you talk to is the one who would run the project, and your answers arrive with the booking so the thirty minutes goes on your project rather than on the same eight questions.

faqs.question: Does a faster launch always cost more?
faqs.answer: Only when it compresses the schedule. A launch inside eight weeks adds 15 to 20 per cent, because design and build have to overlap and more of the team is on the project at once. About four months or longer adds nothing, because that is the pace a focused build or a platform build runs at anyway.

faqs.question: What makes an online store cost more than a marketing site?
faqs.answer: Checkout, payments, stock and the operational work behind them. A marketing site has to explain and convert; a store also has to take money reliably, keep prices and stock in step with whatever system runs the business, and handle returns and reconciliation without anyone re-keying an order. That is why the starting figure for a store is higher, and why connecting an inventory or ERP system is the largest single addition in the table above.
